To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PVA is a visual analytics approach that (1) uses partial results of a computation, (2) shows them to the user for interaction, (3) and thereby supports the user’s decision-making process.

PVA is a design paradigm for interactive visual analytics that (1) allows users to interact with the computation of an end result, and that (2) is characterized by the following four key concepts: (2a) progressive computation, (2b) incremental visualization, (2c) user interaction, and (2d) feedback.

(1) PVA is an umbrella term that covers various approaches and instantiations, (2) it is characterized by a set of fundamental concepts, and (3) it can be used for various applications, but requires a careful consideration of a set of specific requirements.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: “What is progressive visual analytics?”.
the identification, characterization, and systematization of the core concepts of PVA.
the following questions: What is PVA?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PVA is a research area in its own right, with many different facets, that has been around for a long time and has been used successfully in a variety of different domains.

progressive visualization and progressive analytics are not the same, that PVA is not just about visual analytics, that PVA has to be understood as an approach to visual analytics, and that PVA is a research domain that is still in the making.
PVA is a research area that is currently in the process of being defined and that has not yet reached the stage of maturity where it can be clearly distinguished from other visual analytics concepts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a review and characterization of PVA that helps to better understand the fundamental concepts of this field and to identify the most important design considerations for its implementation.
PVA is a research area that is not only about progressive computation, but also about progressive visualization.
we have identified the key elements of PVA, discussed their interplay in detail and presented a characterization that is based on the existing body of research.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to be successful, PVA requires a holistic view of the entire process from problem formulation to the end result.
PVA is not a specific technology but an overarching concept that can be applied to a wide variety of different technologies, methods, and algorithms.
the term progressive visual analytics should be used in a more narrow sense than it has been used in the past.
